host.note: Apple silicon; hardware TSO available but NOT requested by box64, so the CPU runs in weak memory order

backendReason: box64 works natively on 16K pages and needs no rootfs or patchelf; FEX would require muvm and is blocked by muvm#240 on this kernel

renderer.note: bridged natively by box64; the guest never loads an x86_64 GL driver

BOX64_PREFER_WRAPPED.reason: Bridge native GL/X11/SDL2 rather than emulate them. Required because every RUNPATH lookup contains a '/', which otherwise makes box64's `precise` check skip the native wrapper.

BOX64_NORCFILES.reason: Seal (D13, PLAN2 §7). The only way to stop a user's ~/.box64rc from silently section-replacing propnix's tuning. No rcfile exists on this host, so it changes nothing today — it prevents a future surprise.

SDL_VIDEODRIVER.reason: Keeps SDL off the Wayland backend. Part of the author's independently-established working configuration, and RE-TESTED 2026-08-07: wayland still fails. See waylandRetest below. This is Unity-specific and NOT a general default — stellaris-x86_64.nix prefers wayland on the same host (RESEARCH §17).

gameArgs.reason: MANDATORY. Without it Unity selects a renderer that dies during scene load: black screen, audio playing, then SIGILL. Not derivable by any static analysis — this is the single most important hand-found setting.

notSet.BOX64_UNITY: Tried and removed. Present in an earlier attempt that crashed; not part of the verified-working configuration, so it is not carried.
notSet.BOX64_DYNAREC_STRONGMEM: Tried on the hypothesis that weak memory order caused the crash. It did not; the cause was the renderer flag. Left unset rather than kept as cargo cult — but see PLAN2 §7.1: never set it to 0 on the grounds that the hardware has TSO, because box64 never requests TSO.
notSet.patchelf: Not needed. box64 is the loader and ignores the ELF interpreter.

libraries.model: union of two sets; neither alone is sufficient
libraries.bridgingNativeReason: sonames box64 wraps; the NATIVE aarch64 copy must be present for box64 to dlopen and bridge it
libraries.guestOnlyX86Reason: the payload's verified DT_NEEDED closure, which box64 does not wrap
libraries.note: The author's original hand-written wrapper listed only the bridging set and worked because it APPENDED to an inherited LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Sealing the environment removed that crutch and forced the full list to be explicit — the seal earning its keep.

payload.sizeNote: GOG's API size is WRONG by 262055 bytes. Never use it as an integrity gate; only the hash is authoritative.
payload.credentialChannel: extra-sandbox-paths bind mount at /propnix, granted via `setfacl -m g:nixbld:r`
payload.layout: data/noarch/game — there is no data/x86_64 tree

propnixRevNote: not yet a git repository; this record predates version control

singleInstance.reason: Unity runs in SingleInstance mode and cannot create unity.lock in the read-only store game directory; it logs 'Read-only file system' and continues unprotected

knownIssues: Every launch logs 'Error opening <store>/unity.lock: Read-only file system'. Cosmetic — the flock guard provides the protection Unity wanted.
The game runs from the read-only store, so anything expecting a writable game directory would fail. Nothing in Hollow Knight does; saves go to ~/.config/unity3d.
notMeasured: fps — no frame-rate measurement was taken, so this record cannot support any performance claim
sustained play — verified reaching gameplay and writing a save, not a long session
whether the older save that originally failed to load works now; a new game was used instead

waylandRetest.observed: reaches `Renderer: Apple M2 (G14G B0)` and `OPENGL LOG: Creating OpenGL 4.6 graphics device`, loads the physics module, then `a fatal error in the mono runtime or one of the native libraries` and SIGILL (exit 132, core dumped).
waylandRetest.redHerring: the wayland path additionally loads the payload's bundled libdecor-0.so.0, which x11 never touches, and under BOX64_PREFER_WRAPPED=1 box64 tries to bridge it natively along with libdbus-1 and libz — all three fail because this package supplies no native copy of them. Supplying native libdecor, dbus and zlib removed every `Error initializing native` line and produced the IDENTICAL Mono SIGILL, so the bridge failures are a symptom, not the cause.
waylandRetest.conclusion: x11 stays. The cause is Unity's Mono under box64 on the wayland path and is unexplained; no library change fixes it, so no library change was carried.

nativeVsEmulated.claim: on the shipping x11 configuration, every system library the game uses is already native aarch64 — there is nothing left to convert
nativeVsEmulated.method: ELF machine byte (offset 18) of every file-backed .so mapping in /proc/<pid>/maps, sampled after the renderer came up. box64's `Using native(wrapped)` line at BOX64_LOG=1 is not sufficient: it covers only the initial DT_NEEDED walk, showing 9 libraries where the process actually maps 69.
nativeVsEmulated.measured: 69 file-backed shared objects mapped, ALL AArch64, zero x86-64. Includes libGL/libGLX_mesa/libgallium/libLLVM, libX11/libxcb*, libXcursor/libXext/libXfixes/libXi/libXinerama/libXrandr/libXrender/libXss/libXxf86vm, libpulse*, libdbus-1, libudev, libz, libsystemd, libdrm*.
nativeVsEmulated.emulatedRemainder: UnityPlayer.so and the bundled Mono runtime — the game's own code, which has no native equivalent. box64 reports these as `Using emulated`.
